newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico labor boss asked to cut down work by doctor.
newsitem.headline: Mexico labor boss asked to cut down work by doctor.

text.p: Mexico's 97-year-old labor baron, Fidel Velazquez, has been pressured by his doctor to cut down his work schedule as head of the giant Confederation of Mexican Workers (CTM) after repeated spells in hospital.

"I haven't recommended that Don Fidel should retire...I think that if he moderates his work schedule, if he works half days, if he goes just four days a week, for example, then he could continue doing some work in the CTM," his doctor, Salomon Jasqui, told a news conference.

Velazquez, who has dominated the pro-government labor sector for half a century, was expected to stay in a military hospital at least until Sunday to get over the worst of his urinary tract infection.
Jasqui said he expected him to take another week of rest at home before going back to his office at the CTM.

The doctor said the labor leader is determined to reach his hundredth birthday. But he has been in and out of hospital repeatedly this year and during his latest illness he has shed 22 pounds (10 kg).
